note: Wisconsin DNR champion register plus Lake Park Friends Tree Walk (2016) and DNR Every Root an Anchor excerpts. Pass 2026-11-04.

leads.name: Lake Park swamp white oak at the Locust Street turn-around
leads.reason: Lake Park Friends Tree Walk 2016 stop 31 says almost 200 years old, grass triangle behind the Locust Street turn-around; same park as mke_004/005, not delivered only to avoid a fourth near-duplicate oak; add if the page wants it, source https://lakeparkfriends.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/LPF-Tree-Book-2016.pdf

leads.name: Lake Park trail-marker white ashes near the Indian mound
leads.reason: Friends say about 200 years old and bent by Native Americans as trail markers (a legend); ash in Milwaukee County is being removed for emerald ash borer, so alive-now unknown

leads.name: Lake Park champion European beech near the Brick Arch Bridge
leads.reason: 2011 circ 149 in; Friends appendix may mark it CUT DOWN IN 2016 (layout ambiguous); verify on site before use

leads.name: Lake Park European ashes by Lake Drive
leads.reason: 2011 circ 95 in and 86 in, once state record, EAB risk, location only 'LK Dr'; a CC0 iNaturalist observation 2025-07-11 at 43.0734,-87.8701 (297014673) is needs_id, not confirmed as this tree

leads.name: Whitnall Park sugar maple over 270 years old
leads.reason: DNR Every Root an Anchor excerpt (Whitnall Park and Boerner Gardens, 88) says near the corner of Grange Avenue and Root River Parkway Drive, Hales Corners; old book text, no coordinate, no alive confirmation; the best old-tree lead in the county, needs a modern source

leads.name: Oak Creek shagbark hickory (DNR champion objectid 3023)
leads.reason: 108 in, 105 ft; register coordinate 42.89415,-87.94296 lands beside a residential street (S 20th St), 'north of the water tower at the north end of a hardwood forest'; public land not shown, no alive evidence; no photo or exact pin in reach

leads.name: Boerner Botanical Gardens Scots pines
leads.reason: DNR excerpt: planted about 100 years before the book, nucleus of the conifer collection on 92nd Street near College Avenue; garden is paid entry; no tree-level source or coordinate
